title: kbgit.py knows its remotes by role
goal: kbpublic.py resolves both remote roles: integration_remote() reads git config kb.integrationRemote (default origin) and publish_remote() keeps reading kb.publishRemote (unset: no public home); kbgit.py sync and the pre-push hook, kbgit.py publish, backlog.py red-pipeline and ql_deliver.py take the integration remote from it and --remote/--source still override; no _tools/*.py other than kbpublic.py and the tests holds the string constant 'origin' or 'origin/...'; tests.py -k TestRemoteRoles covers a clone whose integration remote is not named origin, with and without a publish remote

gates.question: Where does a clone record its remote roles?
options: git config kb.integrationRemote (default origin) beside the existing kb.publishRemote, per clone, never committed
a committed file naming the remotes
fixed names by convention (origin, and one name for the public home)
gates.recommendation: git config kb.integrationRemote (default origin) beside the existing kb.publishRemote, per clone, never committed
gates.answer: git config kb.integrationRemote (default origin) beside the existing kb.publishRemote, per clone, never committed

notes: kb.publishRemote exists already (kbpublic.CONFIG_KEY; maintaining.md setup step 4; .githooks/pre-push reads it when Python is missing), so only the integration role is new. kbpublic.py is already imported by kbgit.py and ql_deliver.py; backlog.py imports it lazily as it does ql_deliver. ql_deliver.origin_forge keeps reading the forge from the remote's url (red-pipeline and the query log's CI check need it): roles name remotes, not hosts.
